nodes.title: ElevenLabs Agents public teardown (account-free): 56 graded claims from the 804-page docs index (258 page bodies saved as Markdown), the public OpenAPI (322 paths, 141 convai), pricing pages, 32 changelog entries, the incident.io status feed, 6 npm SDKs and the PyPI SDK, DNS/RDAP of 19 hostnames, passive captures of elevenlabs.io/agents and the signed-out app, one 25 s public demo call, 157 job posts, Trustpilot, GitHub issues and HN. Adversarially verified the same day: 37 claims re-checked, 2 downgraded to unknown (EL-21 Iowa media anchoring; EL-33 82-97% margin), 1 sub-claim refuted (EL-23 embeddings are intfloat open weights), 15 corrected or scoped. Grades now 44 observed, 7 inferred, 3 vendor-claimed, 2 unknown. sha256 manifest of 3,846 raw files.

ElevenLabs is building a lead-level outbound campaign product that is not public yet. The signed-out dashboard bundle carries a generated client for 16 unpublished /v1/convai/outbound-campaigns paths (18 operations): campaigns submit/pause/resume/stop/progress/calls/export, leads with useSuppressLead (DELETE a lead), an attention queue (resolve/retry), workspace config and pre-revoke-status, plus a dashboard page route /outbound-campaigns. Public conversation records already carry batch-call campaign metadata {campaign_id, campaign_lead_id, cold_attempt, conversation_type initial/retry/callback/redirect} (2026-08-31). The public product is still single-start batch calling with no calling window, retry policy or suppression. Of 335 unique convai/speech-engine paths in the bundle, 204 (243 operations) are absent from the public OpenAPI, including automations, task-agents, memories, templates and analytics queries. Counts re-done by the verifier with dedupe by normalised path; the lane first reported 23 and 326 of 568 because paths seen by both regexes were counted twice.

ElevenLabs has an India data-residency environment, but only on Enterprise. The 2026-10-17 parity row "no India region found" is wrong. in.residency.elevenlabs.io is a separate, blank workspace with limited migration; storage is in India, "processing may nevertheless occur outside", and Realtime v1 Max is not offered there. Observed: SIP signalling is regional. sip.rtc.elevenlabs.io is one GCP us-central1 IP and sip.rtc.in.residency.elevenlabs.io is asia-south1 (Mumbai). The answer is the same for Jio, Airtel and Azure Central India client subnets (ECS scope /0, no geo-DNS), and the static-IP SIP /24 (199.88.252.0/24) is registered to Eleven Labs Inc. Vendor-claimed: standard-workspace data and self-hosted LLMs are in the US, and residency "may" reduce latency. Unknown (verifier downgrade of EL-21): where RTP media and the agent runtime run for a standard Indian buyer, since the docs say SIP servers are distributed and RTP uses dynamic IPs, and so whether a ~200-250 ms India-US penalty per turn exists. EL-P08 measures it.

Exotel has been a first-class ElevenAgents telephony provider since 2026-06-01, alongside Twilio and SIP. Exotel's Voicebot applet streams 8 kHz PCM over a WebSocket to ElevenLabs; outbound uses Exotel Calls/connect with the buyer's own keys; the Mumbai and Singapore clusters are supported. Friction: Exotel support must first enable the gated Voicebot applet and provision channels (1-2 business days), and transfer needs a chained Connect applet. This is the self-serve route to a domestic Indian CLI that Vapi lacks. The India page also claims Ozonetel and Plivo integrations and Indian agent customers (Meesho, Cars24, TVS Motor; vendor-claimed).

ElevenAgents leaves Indian calling compliance to the buyer. The 258 saved docs pages never mention TRAI, DLT, NCPR/DND, the 140/160 series or Indian calling hours; the only telemarketing-law page is TCPA. The public batch API has no calling-window, DNC, consent or suppression field. AI disclosure and recording consent are contractual duties of the buyer. Twilio regional routing offers only us1/ie1/au1.

ElevenAgents all-in list price for an Indian outbound minute at FX 95: INR 8.17-8.92 via Exotel or Plivo, INR 15.8-16.5 in burst, INR 12.5-15.0 via Twilio. The platform fee is $0.08 = INR 7.60 on every plan, unchanged in USD since 2026-06-06, and alone is above the INR 3.5-7 Indian band (2.1-2.6x Sarvam all-in). The rest is LLM pass-through (INR 0.19-0.72, flash-lite rows; the default gemini-2.5-flash is not priced) and telephony (INR 0.38-0.60; Exotel is quote-gated and assumed equal to Plivo, and the Plivo route may be closed on a standard US-SIP workspace because Indian numbers need media anchored in India). The $0.08 fee is 3.3-3.9x the same ASR and TTS on ElevenLabs' own API list. A reconstructed-COGS margin (82-97%) is an analogue hypothesis that the verifier downgraded to unknown (EL-33).

nodes.title: ElevenLabs velocity and reliability. From 2026-04-01 to 2026-10-12 there were 32 changelog entries (about weekly) with 296 headline items, 195 of them for ElevenAgents (median 6 per entry), plus weekly SDK releases (JS/Python 2.74 on 2026-10-20). The status feed (incident.io) shows 25 incidents from 2026-07-31 to 2026-10-13: 9 name Agents, SIP, Twilio, batch calling or conversation history, 4 are SIP/Twilio telephony and 5 are EU-residency.
nodes.method: elevenlabs.io/docs/changelog/llms.txt and each entry .md (items counted per section by code), status.elevenlabs.io/feed.rss parsed; fetched 2026-10-20

nodes.title:
ElevenLabs v2 signals.
- Memory across calls has no feature docs. The only public mention is "user memories" under agent privacy settings in the versioning doc; the public PrivacyConfig has no memory field. The data model has memory entries (version, conversation/manual source, since 2026-04-27), and the dashboard calls /agents/{id}/memories and /agents/{id}/user-memory/preview.
- On widget traffic the default user_id is a FingerprintJS browser fingerprint (persisted in localStorage), so any per-user memory there is keyed to a device, not an authenticated person.
- Personalisation today is per call only: dynamic variables, overrides, user_id and initiation webhooks.
- The improvement loop is human-gated: Spotlight finds an issue, Architect proposes a branch with tests, a teammate merges, and experiments split traffic with manual promotion and no documented significance test.
- "Proactive proposals" and scheduled automations are announced; the bundle already calls /convai/automations and /triage-tickets/{id}/architect-dispatches.

nodes.rationale: Public evidence shows ElevenLabs owns the speech stack (ASR, TTS, turn model, S2S; embeddings are open weights), ships ~6 agent features a week, already offers domestic Indian telephony through Exotel (after a 1-2 business-day applet enablement), and has a leads/suppression/retries campaign product built but unpublished. Its margin is unknown: an analogue COGS estimate suggests room to cut price, but the verifier graded it unknown. Its public gaps for Indian outbound are India-region processing for self-serve buyers (the latency effect is unmeasured), Indian compliance controls, Hinglish handling on a configured agent (unmeasured; the public demo forces English) and India-specific failure reasons.
nodes.reverse_if: ElevenLabs makes outbound campaigns public with calling windows and suppression and offers India-region processing on self-serve plans; or the account phase measures handset p50 <= 1.5 s with >= 90% Hinglish language hold on the default configuration; or it prices Indian minutes at or below INR 4 all-in.

nodes.title: Within about one quarter, ElevenLabs could launch its hidden outbound-campaigns product (leads, retries, suppression) and cross-call memory, and cut its Indian price toward INR 4/min. Its margin is unknown (an analogue estimate of 82-97% was downgraded to unknown by the verifier), so how cheap a cut would be is unknown too. That would close the usability and price gaps VP is targeting, leaving India-resident latency (unmeasured), compliance and Hinglish quality.
nodes.mitigation: Re-run code/bundle_endpoints.py weekly against the signed-out app bundle and the public OpenAPI (radar watchlist), deduping by normalised path (code/verify_bundle_check.py), and diff the changelog. Build VP's Indian operator layer (DLT/140-160 declaration, NCPR scrub, consent ledger, IST windows, business-language outcomes) as the product, and keep India-resident processing on every plan.

nodes.title:
Do the pre-registered ElevenLabs account-phase predictions EL-P01 to EL-P12 hold?
- Web call within 10 min, but an Indian-handset call takes >= 30 min via Twilio and >= 1 business day via Exotel.
- The CSV keeps duplicates and the opt-out row and does not prefix +91.
- There is no calling window.
- LLM voicemail detection misses Indian operator announcements.
- Handset reply gap p50 is 2.0-3.2 s on a standard plan.
- There is no cross-call memory by default.
nodes.closes_when: An ElevenLabs trial (the existing free account from the Instinct report, plus an Exotel or Twilio number) runs EL-P01 to EL-P12. That needs timed screen recordings, the 50-row CSV outcome per row, a scheduling attempt, three Indian operator announcements, the l4b battery on our Plivo/Exotel number (>= 30 clean turns, stereo), the invoice lines, and a check whether outbound-campaigns or memory is visible in the workspace. Before the run, apply the verifier's fixes (verify.md): pre-register a configured-agent (hi + Hindi voice + language detection) language-hold companion to EL-P02 with a coding rule; define "mishandled" per category for EL-P03 and EL-P11; score EL-P08 separately for the Exotel (WebSocket) and SIP routes, with its residency clause not-testable without Enterprise; add the 5% silence rate to EL-P10.

nodes.title: Reusable unreleased-feature detector. bundle_endpoints.py pulls the generated API-client routes out of a signed-out dashboard's JS, using string matching only (nothing is executed), and diffs them against the vendor's public OpenAPI. With capture.mjs, har_scripts.py and har_slim.py it turns one passive sign-in page load into a list of unpublished product surfaces.
nodes.value: Found ElevenLabs outbound-campaigns (16 paths), memories, automations and task-agents (204 unpublished unique paths) before any announcement. It runs weekly as change-watch on any vendor whose dashboard ships a generated client (Fern, OpenAPI codegen). Known bug: bundle_endpoints.py keys (method,path) and ("?",path) separately, so any path seen by both regexes is counted twice. Report counts deduped by normalised path, as verify_bundle_check.py does.
nodes.effort: about 1 minute per vendor per run, with no account

nodes.title: Adversarial verification of the ElevenLabs lane: 37 of 56 claims re-checked against their files plus fresh public re-captures. Two inferences were downgraded to unknown: Iowa media anchoring with a ~200-250 ms India penalty (EL-21), and an 82-97% platform margin (EL-33). One sub-claim was refuted: RAG embeddings are intfloat E5 open weights, not ElevenLabs' own. Hidden-route counts were corrected (16 campaign paths, 204 unpublished paths; bundle_endpoints.py double-counts). New observations: no geo-DNS on SIP for Indian subnets; livekit-server behind GCP LBs; the widget uses a browser fingerprint as user_id; the public demo forces language "en", so English replies there test the page, not the platform. Predictions are falsifiable; EL-P02, P03, P08, P10 and P11 need sharpening before the run. Inference.

events.details: Adversarial verifier re-checked 37 of 56 ElevenLabs claims. Two were downgraded to unknown (EL-21, EL-33), one sub-claim refuted (EL-23), 15 corrected or scoped, 18 confirmed as written; none was refuted whole, so no node was removed. claims.json was edited in place (verify blocks keep the original text). Inbox nodes corrected: SIP region, hidden campaigns, all-in price, v2 memory, decision rationale, risk, open-question, asset (renamed to the lane id convention). The lane never wrote report.md, and the verifier's attempt to create it was blocked by the harness; verify.md is the Verification section of record. Re-captures are in data/teardown/elevenlabs/verify-2026-10-20/ (37 files, in manifest.csv).
